description: Apply the neuroscience concept of predictive coding to DEFLATE decompression. In the visual cortex, higher layers predict lower-layer activity and only prediction errors are transmitted. Analogously, predict the next Huffman symbol (most likely = most common literal) and speculatively decode assuming the prediction is correct. Only pay full decode cost when the prediction fails.
mathematical_formalization: Let p_max = probability of most common symbol, len_max = its Huffman code length. Speculative decode cost C_spec = len_max. Correction cost C_corr = T_full_decode * (1 - p_max). Expected cost E[C] = C_spec + C_corr = len_max + T_full * (1 - p_max). Beneficial when p_max > 1 - len_max/T_full.
analogical_connections: Visual cortex predictive coding: predict expected stimuli, only process surprises
Branch prediction in CPUs: speculatively execute the predicted branch
Delta encoding in video codecs: encode only differences from predicted frame
implementation_hypothesis: Profile symbol frequency distribution. If a single literal has probability > 30%, create a speculative fast-path: peek at the next len_max bits, check if they match the predicted symbol's code. If match, emit and advance (2-3 cycles). If mismatch, fall through to full table-lookup (~7 cycles).
experiment_seed: Collect symbol frequency histograms across diverse file types. Compute potential speedup for speculative decode with top-1, top-2, top-3 predictions. Implement and benchmark on files with skewed distributions.
